newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African truth body orders ANC bombers to testify.
newsitem.headline: S.African truth body orders ANC bombers to testify.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission said on Sunday it had issued its first summonses compelling former guerrillas of the African National Congress to testify about attacks during the war against apartheid.

A statement from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu said subpoenas had been sent to Robert McBride and Greta Appelgren who set off a car bomb outside a bar in Durban in 1985, killing three white civilians.

McBride was sentenced to death for the attack but this was commuted to life imprisonment and he was freed under an amnesty for political prisoners before South Africa's first democratic elections in 1994. Appelgren received a lesser sentence.

McBride, who holds a job in the department of foreign affairs, has said his commanders in the ANC -- now the ruling party -- told him to bomb the bar. But he has so far refused to name those who gave the orders.

The truth commission statement said McBride would be questioned among other things about ..."the extent of the involvement of the military and political wing of the ANC in the planning and execution of the bombing".

The law setting up the commission, which is intended to unveil human rights abuses and other crimes from the apartheid era, provides for jail terms for anyone who defies a subpoena or refuses to answer questions satisfactorily.
The commission has previously subpoenaed only former members of the white-led security forces, prompting accusations by right-wing critics that it is conducting a witch hunt.

Local newspapers reported on Sunday that ANC leaders had objected to the subpoenas served on former guerrillas because the information sought by the commission was due to be provided by the party in a separate submission.
Tutu, who is being treated for prostate cancer, has said the commission will rule in its final report on whether it believed the ANC had been justified in taking up arms against apartheid.
